definition: Committing to one line of attack before the alternatives have been explored, which from the outside looks like confidence. Across 3 sources it is measurable in three different places. In a trace: the pattern of high initial and high final confidence, which a confidence-maximising selector preferentially picks -- so uniformly high confidence indicates a failure to branch rather than a well-supported answer, and maximisation can perform below random selection. In a calibration table: the highest-agreement bin being correct about half the time for one model and less often than its own lowest bin for another, so agreement does not track correctness on hard problems. And in a search policy: agents following a monotonic zoom-in once a region is chosen, unable to recover from an early wrong commitment. The remedy the sources share is to score the temporal shape rather than the level -- penalising early certainty while requiring late certainty -- or to make revision a first-class action.

evidence.note: Replaces the monotonic zoom-in that tool-using video agents follow once they pick a region with a policy that self-checks each tool observation and can switch regions, and trains it with turn-level credit applied multiplicatively -- reweighting the trajectory advantage's magnitude while preserving its sign -- rather than additively.
evidence.title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning

evidence.note: Shows that selecting the most confident rollout can be worse than picking at random, because uniformly high confidence signals a failure to explore rather than a well-supported answer, and replaces maximisation with a temporal criterion that penalises early certainty while requiring late certainty.
evidence.title: Consilience for Verifier-Free Test-Time Scaling

evidence.note: Measures, under a pre-registered confirmatory design, how often majority-vote self-consistency lowers per-problem accuracy on a hard science benchmark, and shows that two cheap verifier-free gates recover essentially none of the headroom a per-problem oracle marks out.
evidence.title: When Self-Consistency Backfires: Majority Vote Hurts the Majority of Hard Science Problems for Small LLMs

name: premature convergence
